question: Will the world's population keep growing for ever?
answer: Not by the UN's projections, which have it levelling off around ten or eleven billion by 2100. Rosling's reason: the number of children in the world has already stopped growing. Families have fewer children as they leave extreme poverty; the billions still to come are mostly adults living longer.
move: Most lines bend: ask what will bend this one before you extend it.
simply: A tree grows fast when it is young and slows down when it is big. Drawing a straight line from its first years would make it reach the clouds.
why: Straight-line forecasts make every trend look like a crisis. Finding what bends a curve is how you plan for what will actually happen.
reference: Hans Rosling, Ola Rosling and Anna Rosling Rönnlund, Factfulness (Flatiron Books, 2018), ch. 3
